headline: Rescinded the council president vote, elected a new president, and approved development agreements for Bates Mill #5 and Eco Hospitality Consultants.
summary: The council held several public hearings and approved ordinance changes on rental registration, outdoor entertainment permits, business license definitions, and the No Name Pond Conservation Overlay District. It rescinded the January 2026 vote for council president, elected Councilor Nagine as the new president, approved agreements for the Bates Mill #5 redevelopment and Eco Hospitality Consultants project, and approved the sale of 11 King Avenue. It also voted to place a Charter Commission question on the November ballot and postponed a request for an additional agency liquor store license.
decisions: Appointed Emily Levasseur to the vacant Ward 7 seat on the School Committee, effective July 21, 2026, term ending January 4, 2027.
Confirmed Julia Bartlett as the Financial Institution Representative on the Housing Committee, three-year term expiring January 2, 2029.
Approved a new liquor license and special amusement permit for The Colisee, 190 Birch Street.
Granted an outdoor entertainment permit to the Dempsey Center for the Dempsey Challenge at Simard-Payne Park, September 13-22.
Gave final passage to create Chapter 23 'Residential Rental Properties' and add rental registration language.
Gave final passage to remove rental registration language from Chapter 18 'Buildings & Building Regulations'.
Gave final passage to amend Chapter 10 'Amusements and Entertainment' to remove the public hearing requirement for outdoor entertainment permits and let staff issue them.
Gave final passage to amend Chapter 22 'Businesses' Section 22-422 to remove the list of city parks.
Gave final passage to amend the Zoning and Land Use Code for the No Name Pond Conservation Overlay District to require buffer disturbance to follow DEP requirements.
Amended the proposed Solid Waste ordinance to raise the container weight limit to 250 pounds and make other wording changes.
Gave first passage to the Solid Waste ordinance amendment defining the automated side load trash collection program and continued the public hearing to the next meeting.
Approved the Letter of Intent with Eco Hospitality Consultants for redevelopment projects including the Red Shop and hotel expansion.
Authorized the City Administrator to execute an Option Agreement with Bates Mill, LLC for Bates Mill #5, granting an exclusive purchase option through June 30, 2031.
Rescinded City Council Vote 12-2026 from the January 5, 2026 meeting, which had elected the 2026 Council President.
Elected Councilor Nagine as City Council President for the remainder of the term, ending January 4, 2027.
Approved placing a Charter Commission question on the November 2026 ballot asking voters whether to establish a new municipal charter.
Postponed the request for an additional agency liquor store license to the next Council meeting.
Approved the disposition of 11 King Avenue to Peer Property Management LLC for $55,000.

CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
 
REGULAR MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 7:00 P.M. 
 
THE HONORABLE CARL L. SHELINE, MAYOR, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Mayor Sheline, Councilors Nagine, Longchamps, Harriman, Roy, Noble, Chittim, 
and Martel, City Administrator Bryan Kaenrath, Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley, and 
City Clerk Kathleen Montejo.  
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
VOTE (263-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
  
To dispense with the reading of the minutes of the meetings of June 30 and July 7, 2026, and to 
accept and place them on file as prepared by the City Clerk.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
Ronnie Paradis, Ward 6 – Thank you to city, the groundbreaking for the new senior housing at 
Martel School was excellent. Thank you to Councilor Nagine for updating social media about the 
large apartment fire, the city did not do that. Would like people to start talking about issues and 
not people especially in regard to the recent youth gun violence. Adults need to set an example 
for kids, say nice things about each other, discuss policies and not people. 
 
Andrew Jones, Ward 2 – Compliments to the City Clerk on her knowledge of parliamentary 
procedure and assisting with the meetings. Thank you to Councilor Noble for speaking up 
against the Council President’s actions at the last meeting. Councilor Chittim should not engage 
in double-dealing behind the scenes, this loses trust. A member of the Safety Committee 
organized a dog walk, and recommended people leave out dog treats with laxatives to poison the 
animals, the Council should address this. 
 
Matt Agren, Ward 4 – Pleased to be at the Martel School groundbreaking. Good response from 
the city to set up the emergency shelter for the apartment fire victims. All Councilors need to 
find common ground, everyone was elected to represent their ward, but the whole of Lewiston 
needs everyone’s help with public safety. Excited about plans in the works to create one 
department on the third floor, Economic Development should focus on ten projects with 20 jobs 
each, not one project with 200 jobs. 
 
David Racknells, Ward 1 – It has been a busy year for the city, thank you to Councilors for being 
part of the team.  You don’t compete against each other; you need to talk to each other and work 
together. Accountability works but need more dialogue, keep respectful during meetings. If 
problems can’t be discussed, they cannot be addressed. 
 
Kim Bush, Ward 2 – Lives on Walnut Street.  There is so much chaos, cannot sleep at night. A
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
2 
 
friend was shot in the face a few weeks ago, not a random act of violence but targeted. People 
are too scared to talk with police.  
 
Charles Soule, 70 Horton Street – Was at Challenger Drive for this morning for an appointment 
with a doctor at the veterans’ clinic and tractor trailer trucks were parked on both sides of the 
road. There were pallets and trash along the side of the road. It should be no parking on one side. 
Lewiston should create our own jail system. 
 
Jon Horton, Ward 2 – Mobile Home park owner – the upcoming rent control ordinance is the 
wrong thing to do and it not a business-friendly move. Living in a mobile home park is the most 
affordable way of living. Parks will not be expanding due to new ordinance. Try to apply 
proposed limits of CPI limit to city operations. The committee working on the ordinance has 
been professional and he appreciates that. 
 
Nathan, Lewiston – Country capable of building skyscrapers but letting citizens become 
homeless. 
 
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT 
 
Another Cart to Curb information session is coming up. Congratulations to employees on recent 
promotions and retirements. The Maine Resiliency Center has opened their community survey. 
The Beyond the Badget event will be held Thursday afternoon in Simard-Payne Memorial Park. 
The renovation of the high school tennis courts is complete. The state Lobster Bowl Classic 
football game was recently held at the Lewiston High School fields. Thank you to members of 
the No Name Pond Association for hosting the City Administrator on a recent boat ride of the 
Pond and for discussing watershed issues.  
 
 
CONFIRMATION OF MAYOR SHELINE’S NOMINATION TO FILL THE CURRENT 
VACANCY IN THE WARD 7 POSITION ON THE SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
 
Emily Levasseur, Ward 7, introduced herself and noted she is the mother of two young children 
who are neurodivergent, her husband is a disabled veteran, and she is a small business owner 
who is also a five-year behavioral health professional. Seirra Pomerleau, Ward 7 – Has known 
Ms. Levasseur for ten years and spoke in support of her appointment. 
 
VOTE (264-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Harriman: 
 
To receive the Mayor’s nomination and to appoint Emily Levasseur to fill the vacant Ward 7 
position on the Lewiston School Committee, said appointment to be effective as of July 21, 
2026, with a term ending January 4, 2027.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
 
APPOINTMENT OF THE FINANCIAL INSTITUTION REPRESENTATIVE TO THE 
HOUSING COMMITTEE
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
3 
 
VOTE (265-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Harriman, seconded by Councilor Chittim: 
 
To receive the Mayor’s appointment and to confirm the appointment of Julia Bartlett to a three-
year term as the Financial Institution Representative on the Housing Committee, said 
appointment is filling a vacancy and the term will expire January 2, 2029.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING ON AN APPLICATION FOR A NEW LIQUOR LICENSE AND 
SPECIAL AMUSEMENT PERMIT FOR LIVE ENTERTAINMENT FOR 
THE COLISEE, 190 BIRCH STREET 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (266-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To authorize the City Clerk’s Office to approve a new liquor license application and special 
amusement permit for The Colisee, 190 Birch Street. Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING FOR APPROVAL OF AN OUTDOOR ENTERTAINMENT 
PERMIT FOR THE DEMPSEY CHALLENGE 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (267-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
  
To conduct a public hearing on an application for an outdoor entertainment event for the 
Dempsey Challenge, and to grant a permit for an Outdoor Entertainment Event, as required by 
the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 10, Article 1, Section 10-3, to the Dempsey Center for 
outdoor music concerts for the Dempsey Challenge to be held at Simard-Payne Park on 
September 13-22, contingent upon positive recommendations from the Police Department, Fire 
Department, Code/Health Officer, and Land Use Inspector regarding compliance with all 
regulations and compliance with all City ordinances.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE TO ESTABLISH THE RESIDENTIAL 
RENTAL PROPERTIES ORDINANCE AND MOVING THE RENTAL 
REGISTRATION SECTION INTO THIS NEW ORDINANCE 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (268-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel:
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
4 
 
That a new ordinance be created in the City Code of Ordinances designated as Chapter 23 and 
titled “Residential Rental Properties”, and that the proposed amendment to the “Residential 
Rental Properties” ordinance to add the code language regarding the Rental Registration 
program, receive final passage by a roll call vote.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE TO REMOVE THE RENTAL 
REGISTRATION SECTION FROM THE BUILDINGS & BUILDING 
REGULATIONS ORDINANCE 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (269-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the proposed amendment to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 18 “Buildings & 
Building Regulations”, Article VI “Registration Requirement for Multi-Family Buildings”, 
regarding removal of language pertaining to the Rental Registration program, receive final 
passage by a roll call vote.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE REGARDING AN AMENDMENT TO THE 
AMUSEMENTS AND ENTERTAINMENT ORDINANCE TO ELIMINATE THE 
REQUIREMENT FOR A PUBLIC HEARING FOR OUTDOOR ENTERTAINMENT 
PERMITS AND TO AUTHORIZE STAFF TO ISSUE THESE PERMITS 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (270-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Chittim: 
 
That the proposed amendment to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 10 “Amusements and 
Entertainment” to remove the requirement for a public hearing for an Outdoor Entertainment 
Permit and to authorize city staff to issue these permits, receive final passage by a roll call vote. 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE REGARDING AN AMENDMENT TO THE 
BUSINESS LICENSE ORDINANCE TO REMOVE THE LIST OF CITY PARKS AND 
REFER TO THE PARKS AND RECREATION ORDINANCE 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (271-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
That the proposed amendment to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 22 “Businesses”, Section
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
5 
 
22-422 “Definitions” to remove the list of city parks, receive final passage by a roll call vote. 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FINAL PASSAGE FOR AN AMENDMENT TO THE ZONING 
AND LAND USE CODE, ARTICLE XI, DISTRICT REGULATIONS FOR CHANGES 
TO THE NO NAME POND CONSERVATION OVERLAY DISTRICT TO REQUIRE 
SOIL DISTURBANCE WITHIN BUFFERS TO FOLLOW 
MAINE DEP REQUIREMENTS 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. Dave Bernier, 
Ward 6 – Supports a strong, effective ordinance to protect the Pond. Wants to make sure that 18 
Water’s Edge Drive will not be prohibited from construction on the property. The Mayor then 
closed the hearing.  
 
VOTE (272-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the proposed amendments to Appendix A of the Code of Ordinances, Zoning and Land Use 
Code, Article XI, District Regulations for changes to the No Name Pond Conservation Overlay 
District to require disturbance within buffers to follow DEP requirements, receive final passage 
by a roll call vote.  Passed - Vote 7-0 (Councilor Noble was out of the Chambers during the 
vote, the Mayor cast a vote in her absence.) 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST PASSAGE REGARDING AMENDMENTS TO THE 
SOLID WASTE ORDINANCE TO DEFINE THE AUTOMATED SIDE LOAD TRASH 
COLLECTION PROGRAM 
 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing to receive citizen input and comment. No members of 
the public spoke for or against this issue. The Mayor then closed the hearing. City Engineer John 
Kuchinski provided background information for this item.  Councilors discussed several 
amendments and expressed concern with the 50-pound limit per container. 
 
VOTE (273-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Longchamps, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To amend the ordinance to change the weight limit of a container from fifty pounds to up to two 
hundred and fifty pounds, to state the containers must be “at least” two feet apart, and to insert 
the word “that” in Sec 62-6, after the word “establishment”. Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
 
VOTE (274-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
That the proposed amendments to the City Code of Ordinances, Chapter 62 “Solid Waste”, to  
define the automated side load trash collection program, receive first passage by a roll call vote  
and to continue the public hearing to the next regularly scheduled City Council meeting. 
Passed - Vote 7-0
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
6 
 
ORDER, APPROVING THE LETTER OF INTENT WITH ECO 
HOSPITALITY CONSULTANTS 
 
Acting Director of Economic & Community Development John Blais and Developer Chris 
Thompson, made a presentation to the Council on the project and future uses of the park. 
 
VOTE (275-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To adopt the Order, Approving the Letter of Intent with Eco Hospitality Consultants: 
 
Whereas, The proposed Letter of Intent outlines a partnership between the City of Lewiston and  
Eco Hospitality Consultants, Inc. 
 
Whereas, to negotiate a Joint Development Agreement (JDA) focused on four major initiatives:  
redevelopment of the Red Shop into a food, beverage, and event venue; expansion of the existing  
Hampton Inn or construction of a second hotel, and 
 
Whereas, conveyance of the city-owned parcel at 39 Lincoln Street was previously committed  
under a 2011 agreement, and creation of a 30-year Tax Increment Financing (TIF) Credit  
Enhancement Agreement, and  
 
Whereas, the proposal anticipates the Red Shop being sold to the developer for $305,000 or lease  
for an undisclosed amount, while providing the City with a future right to repurchase the property  
under specified conditions, and 
 
Whereas, the developer would also receive enhanced parking rights associated with the City garage 
and pursue additional hotel-related development adjacent to the existing Hampton Inn, and  
 
Whereas, granting the developer a 10 -year exclusive right, with renewal options, to promote 
national touring concerts at Simard -Payne Park. In exchange, the developer would pay the city a 
fee per concert plus applicable public safety and staffing costs. The agreement contemplates a TIF 
district that would return up to 75% of net new tax revenues generated by the project to the 
developer for 30 years.  
 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the City Council of the City of Lewiston, to approve the Order, 
the City Administrator is authorized to execute a Letter of Intent with Eco Hospitality Consultants. 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO EXECUTE AN OPTION 
AGREEMENT WITH BATES MILL, LLC FOR BATES MILL #5 
 
Acting Director of Economic & Community Development John Blais and Developer Tom Platz 
made a presentation to the Council on the future vision for the Mill property.  Elizabeth Eames, 
Ward 3, encouraged a walkway from Simard Payne Park to City Hall.  Matt Roy, Ward 6, said 
in 2007 the Council started kicking the can down the road on this project when they could have
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
7 
 
dealt with it then. They could have torn it down and started over. 
 
VOTE (276-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the Order, Authorizing the City Administrator to execute an Option Agreement with 
Bates Mill, LLC for Bates Mill #5: 
 
Whereas, the City of Lewiston is the owner of the property commonly known as Bates Mill #5; 
and 
Whereas, Bates Mill, LLC has expressed its continued interest in pursuing the redevelopment of 
Bates Mill #5 and advancing planning, financing, tenant recruitment, and redevelopment 
opportunities for the property; and 
Whereas, the proposed Option Agreement grants Bates Mill, LLC an exclusive option to 
purchase Bates Mill #5 through June 30, 2031, while establishing a collaborative redevelopment 
framework between the City and Bates Mill, LLC; and 
Whereas, the Option Agreement includes provisions for redevelopment planning, market 
engagement, financing efforts, biannual progress reporting, and continued collaboration on 
community enhancement initiatives, while recognizing that redevelopment progress is subject to 
market conditions and other factors beyond the developer’s control; and 
Whereas, the City Council finds that entering into the Option Agreement serves a valid public 
purpose by encouraging the long-term redevelopment and productive reuse of Bates Mill #5, 
supporting economic development, job creation, tax base growth, and continued investment 
within the Bates Mill District; 
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the Lewiston City Council that the City Administrator is 
hereby authorized and directed to execute the Option Agreement between the City of Lewiston 
and Bates Mill, LLC, substantially in the form presented to the City Council, together with such 
non-substantive modifications as may be approved by the City Administrator and Corporation 
Counsel. 
Be It Further Ordered that the City Administrator is authorized to execute any documents 
reasonably necessary to implement and administer the Option Agreement consistent with this 
Order. 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, TO RESCIND CITY COUNCIL VOTE 12-2026 TAKEN AT THE MEETING 
OF JANUARY 5, 2026, WHICH WAS FOR THE ELECTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL 
PRESIDENT FOR 2026 
 
Some Councilors expressed concern with the style of Councilor Chittim’s handling of some 
matters.  Councilor Chittim noted he was exploring ideas for alternative funding for the position 
of Economic Development Director, but any final decisions would be brought to the Council. 
Matt Roy, Ward 6, recalls Councilor Chittim saying the Council should pick and choose which
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
8 
 
sections of the Charter to enforce.  Renee Fortin, Ward 6, said it is about building trust and 
working together. Was disappointed at the meeting when Councilor Noble was appointed to hear 
Councilor Chittim say the Council should circumvent the Charter and not follow the advice of 
the City Attorney.  Matt Agren, Ward 4, respects Councilor Chittim because he encourages 
everyone to respect what words mean but his actions show a lack of transparency, lack of 
communication and lack of trust. Peter Geiger, Ward 7, feels that removing Councilor Chittim as 
president is a huge overreaction and people are taking cheap shots at each other. 
 
VOTE (277-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Harriman: 
 
Be It Ordered by the City Council, that the City Council hereby rescinds City Council Vote 12-
2026 taken at the meeting of January 5, 2026, which was for the Election of the City Council 
President for 2026.   Passed - Vote 6-1 (Councilor Chittim opposed) 
 
ELECTION OF CITY COUNCIL PRESIDENT FOR THE REMAINDER OF THIS CITY 
COUNCIL TERM, SAID TERM TO END JANUARY 4, 2027 
 
Councilor Noble nominated Councilor Nagine to the position of Council President. No additional 
nominations were offered. Robert Glasby, Ward 6, encouraged the Council to seek transparency 
and accountability, noting that “Council cohesion” is needed.  
 
VOTE (278-2026) 
 
To elect Councilor Nagine as the City Council President, said term to expire January 4, 2027. 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, PROPOSING THE CREATION OF A CHARTER COMMISSION 
 
Matt Roy, Ward 6, in October 2021, the Council voted to send this matter to the voters, but in 
January 2022, the new Council repealed it. 
 
VOTE (279-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the Order, Proposing the Creation of a Charter Commission: 
 
Whereas the City Council has ordered several proposed amendments to the City Charter to be 
placed on the ballot for voter approval at the November General Election, and 
Whereas these proposed amendments address specific inconsistencies and typographic omissions 
in the Charter, and  
Whereas members of the City Council and the public have, from time to time, advocated for a 
complete review and possible revision of the Charter,
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
9 
 
Now, therefore, it is ordered by the Lewiston City Council, Pursuant to 30-A MRSA § 2102, that 
the following question be put to the voters of Lewiston in the ballot at the November 2026 
General Election “Shall a Charter Commission be established for the purpose of establishing a 
New Municipal Charter?" 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, DIRECTING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO REQUEST AN 
ADDITIONAL AGENCY LIQUOR STORE LICENSE FROM THE MAINE BUREAU 
OF ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES AND LOTTERY OPERATIONS 
 
VOTE (280-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Longchamps, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To postpone this item to the next City Council meeting to allow time to gather additional 
information regarding the request.  Passed - Vote 4-3 (Councilors Harriman, Roy, and Chittim 
opposed) 
 
ORDER, APPROVING THE DISPOSITION OF 11 KING AVENUE 
 
VOTE (281-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Harriman: 
 
To approve the Order, Approving the Disposition of 11 King Avenue: 
 
Whereas, the City Council voted to sell the tax-acquired parcel located at 11 King Avenue at their  
7/15/2025 meeting and 
 
Whereas, the City received multiple offers for the parcel through the City’s Realtor DuBois Realty;  
and 
 
Whereas, Peer Property Management LLC offered $55,000 for 11 King Avenue  
 
Now, T herefore, B e It Ordered by the C ity Council  of the C ity of L ewiston, to approve the 
disposition of 11 King Avenue and authorize the City Administrator to execute all necessary legal 
documents. 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
No additional comments from the public were offered at this time. 
 
REPORTS AND UPDATES 
 
Councilor Nagine noted the Public Health Committee met with representatives from the Maine 
Center for Disease Control regarding a violence intervention program.
CITY COUNCIL  JULY 21, 2026 
                             
10 
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
Councilor Longchamps would like to have an agenda item at the next meeting to review the 
Ethics Policy, specifically as it applies to the appointed members of city boards and committees 
 
VOTE (282-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To adjourn at 9:50 P.M.  Passed - Vote 6-1 (Councilor Chittim opposed) 
 
A true record, Attest: 
 
 
 
Kathleen M. Montejo, MMC  
City Clerk 
Lewiston, Maine
